AMZN.rationale: Amazon's fundamental health is strong: accelerating revenue ($155.67B→$167.70B→$180.17B through Q3 2025), robust cash generation ($35.52B single-quarter OCF in Q3 2025, $85.06B cumulative 9-month), and a fortress balance sheet (D/E 0.149x, equity $369.63B). The franchise is durable with multiple compounding engines—AWS at 28% growth in Q1 2026 ($37.6B revenue), advertising at ~$68.5B run rate growing 22%, and 240M+ Prime members. The Q3 2025 operating margin compression (9.67% vs ~11.5% H1) and non-operating income bridge ($3.77B gap between net and operating income) flagged by the quant report appear to have been resolved: Q1 2026 delivered a record 13.1% companywide operating margin per the qual evidence, suggesting the Q3 2025 dip was temporary. Valuation is the key tension point. The quant pack shows trailing PE at 34.41x (mid-range of 28.2–39.0x), which is not a bargain. However, the qual report's news sources cite forward P/E of ~28x (below S&P 500 average of 32x), and the stock is down ~13% from recent highs, creating a modestly attractive entry relative to the franchise quality. The negative earnings-yield-to-Treasury spread (~159bps) is a headwind, but the 17% YoY revenue growth in Q1 2026 and AWS reacceleration to 28% provide the growth to justify a premium. Near-term catalysts include Q2 2026 earnings (guided $194–199B revenue), the Anthropic IPO filing (Amazon's stake estimated at $135–160B in potential paper value), and AWS GPU price increases of up to 20% signaling pricing power. Risks are real but manageable: $200B 2026 capex compresses near-term FCF, FTC antitrust trial in Oct 2026, and EU regulatory escalation. The broad analyst consensus (57 Buy, 11 Overweight, 0 Sell across 70 ratings) and hedge fund conviction (Ackman, Appaloosa) support the view that structural risks are priced. Score of +0.35 reflects a strong franchise with positive trajectory, modestly attractive valuation after recent pullback, and credible near-term catalysts—above neutral but below +0.5 because the trailing PE is mid-range and the capex cycle creates execution uncertainty.
